knowledge.the_winter_rescue.earthen_smel: Obtaining copper or tin minerals may inspire this idea without prerequisite knowledge. To link, place only a learned raw copper item observation on the tray. Learned clay and sand observations each reduce the wait by one second without tray placement. Starting research requires the idea and all three observations.

1. Prepare: the idea is normally learned automatically. Observe raw copper, a clay ball and sand, keep the records, then learn all three observations at the drawing desk. Start the research. Frozen clay can be thawed at a campfire; rotten wood can be crafted into sticks.
2. Fire a trial: craft clay balls and sand in a 3:1, 1:3 or 2:2 ratio in your 2x2 grid. Place the kiln and right-click with 4 sticks to fire it for 20 seconds. The 2:2 mix stays intact; the other mixes crack. Only one successful sample is required. Start research before adding fuel so the sample belongs to this run.
3. Submit: collect the intact kiln with an empty hand, keep it in your inventory or hotbar and submit it directly in research details (consumes one); the drawing desk item slot also works. Finish the research: both results are normally learned automatically, immediately unlocking brick crafting and smelter formation. Only learn an inbox entry manually if it actually remains there unlearned. Do not inspect or learn the sample itself. Old or cracked samples do not count. You can then craft earthen kiln bricks and form the full earthen smelter with an engineer hammer.
Link a raw copper item observation. Learned clay and sand observations each save one second; keep those auxiliary records off the tray.
Submit this run's intact trial kiln (consumes one)
You can now craft earthen kiln bricks using the existing bricks and structural metal plate recipe. Trial kilns are not an ingredient.

Arrange earthen kiln bricks in the multiblock pattern and form it with an engineer hammer. Finishing this research normally also learns Earthen Kiln Brick Design automatically, unlocking the brick recipe at the same time.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.iron_bloomer: An Idea for Iron Smelting

Obtaining iron minerals or common iron products may inspire this idea without prerequisite knowledge. Link learned item observations of raw iron and one of coal, charcoal or coke. A learned copper or bronze ingot observation saves one second without tray placement. Starting research requires the idea, raw iron, ingot and fuel observations.
Bloomery

Complete the airflow game at the drawing desk, then advance manually to the trial. Winning temporarily unlocks the prototype recipe until this run ends. Finishing normally learns the normal tuyere and main bloomery design automatically. No existing furnace is needed.
Learned copper or bronze ingot observation
Learned coal, charcoal or coke observation
Iron minerals or common iron products
Link raw iron with coal, charcoal or coke item observations. A learned copper or bronze ingot observation saves one second; keep that auxiliary record off the tray.
Bloomery and Tuyere Design

This result is normally learned automatically on completion, unlocking both main bloomery and sandy tuyere recipes. Manually learn it only if it actually remains unlearned in the inbox. Prepare sandy bricks, bronze plates and mortar.
Plan the Airflow
Connect the inlet and outlet
Rotate pipes at the drawing desk to create a continuous path. No paper, ink or score is required.
The path is connected and the prototype recipe is temporarily available. Advance to the next stage.
Connect the airflow
Test the Tuyere
Observe this team and run’s successfully blown tuyere on site

After entering this stage, craft a prototype from one sandy brick block, one bronze plate and one mortar. Place it one block in front of the bellows outlet; replace an earlier placement to bind it. Operate the bellows and wait for its actual blow to turn the prototype into a normal tuyere. No furnace body is needed. Any current member of the bound team can freshly observe that block on site; keeping or learning the observation is not required, and the placer has no personal ownership requirement. If lost, craft and blow another prototype without replaying the game.
The tuyere has passed its airflow trial. Finish research to build a bloomery.

knowledge.the_winter_rescue.refractory_b: An Idea for Refractory Firing

Raw materials, refractory bricks or direct brick products may inspire this idea. To link, place only a learned sandy brick item or sandy brick block item observation on the tray. Learned kaolin, bauxite and clay observations each save one second. Starting research requires the idea, sandy brick and all three material observations. Existing refractory bricks only improve temperature hints.
Ordinary Refractory Bricks

Prepare a stone hammer, tree stump, millstone and campfire. Hand-mix 4 kaolin dust, 4 bauxite dust and 1 clay ball for 1 fire clay ball; mechanical mixing still gives 3. Craft the controlled furnace from 6 clay balls, 2 sand and 1 campfire. Advance to firing, then observe this team and run’s successful brick. No submission, consumption or deliberate failure is required.
Learned kaolin observation
Learned bauxite observation
Learned clay ball observation
Link a sandy brick item or sandy brick block item observation. Learned kaolin, bauxite and clay each save one second; keep those auxiliary records off the tray.
Controlled Refractory Batch Production

Normally learned automatically, this design enables 16 fire clay balls and 2 charcoal to produce 16 ordinary refractory bricks in the controlled furnace. It only unlocks the new batch process. Existing pottery, blast furnace, industrial kiln and block recipes remain unchanged. It does not unlock high refractory bricks or the IE blast furnace.
Prepare Materials and Furnace
Prepare fire clay balls, charcoal and a controlled furnace

Thaw frozen kaolin and bauxite at a campfire. Crush bauxite at the tree stump with a stone hammer, then mill it; kaolin can be milled directly. Hand-mixing uses all nine crafting-table slots. Advance manually when ready; this stage has no required task.
Materials and operation are explained. Advance to freeze the temperature hint for this run.
Fire and Observe
Observe this team and run’s intact ordinary refractory trial brick

Trial mode uses 1 fire clay ball and 1 charcoal. Try the middle of 1000–1200°C; 1100°C is suggested. After 20 seconds, any current team member can freshly observe this run’s successful brick. Do not submit it; keeping or learning the observation is unnecessary. Changes made while running only affect the next firing.

Existing brick observations suggest a successful range of 1050–1150°C inclusive; try 1100°C. Trial mode uses 1 fire clay ball and 1 charcoal for 20 seconds. Any current member of the bound team can freshly observe this run’s successful brick. No archiving or consumption is required.
The ordinary refractory brick has passed its trial. Finish research to enable batch production.
